honesty_note: All 25 WebSearches were real, US-region, executed this session; titles/URLs/snippets recorded verbatim from returned results (some abridged for length, none invented). I deliberately reserved the 4th/5th reformulation of each candidate to attack the MOST SPECIFIC, most-defensible narrowing rather than the easy generic version, to give every candidate its best chance of revealing an unoccupied functional fusion: C07 -> RAG-specific quality-gated pruning; C08 -> dynamic expert proliferation/quiescence and biology-direct framing; C13 -> Lottery-Ticket IMP rewind-to-checkpoint (the closest analog to 'regrow from fixed root stock'); C14 -> per-head subgraph/planar-scaffold binding (HopFormer) and BigBird's long-range-preservation proof; C15 -> the 'small specialists beat one monolith' core efficiency claim. Every narrowing still produced forced functional hits (>=2 declared content_words in title+snippet). Result: 0 of 5 candidates is a genuine non-trivial GAP. This is evidence AGAINST the hypothesis that the sparsest-12 selection missed a real gap in these five less-sparse concepts: each of C07/C08/C13/C14/C15 sits squarely on a populated, named ML technique family (token/KV eviction & pruning; MoE gating; cyclic weight reset / IMP rewinding; structured sparse attention; persistent memory + retrieval-augmented MoE). For C08 and C14 in particular the candidate is essentially a verbatim re-description of a textbook mechanism (MoE gating; fixed-pattern sparse attention), so their higher raw paper-hit counts correctly reflected dense occupation, not a hidden gap. I found no functional fusion that was unoccupied; narrow_version_nontrivial is false for all five.
